prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Make an intimate watercolor GAME PROP DESIGN SHEET, using the attached revised level scene as the exact design reference. Warm ivory paper backdrop, delicate ink drawing and watercolor textures like the reference, generous clear spacing, no decorative borders. Not a game screenshot. Two columns: LEFT is one large close-up of the existing flowerbed-mounted broken garden lantern with its hinged silver reflector; RIGHT is two smaller matched side-profile close-ups of exactly the same beast tail-tip in the same rubble gap, upper unlit, lower first light absorbed.
LEFT: Keep the warm brick flowerbed edge, tiny orange flowers and ivy, old dull corroded iron mounting bracket visibly embedded in masonry, broken lantern cage with missing glass, and its one rectangular FLAT silvered internal backplate hinged at a VERTICAL edge and partly opened like a little door. This reflective plate belongs to the lantern assembly, not an independent floor mirror. Show vertical hinge knuckles clearly. It has fixed mounting tilt and swivels left-right around that upright hinge. A small connected bent iron operating tab descends to near the lower brick ledge, visibly within reach of the tiny light spirit standing on that ledge. The entire spirit is about one lantern-body height: large flame-shaped pale head, tiny body, gold chest. No freestanding pedestal. No electrical wires or modern components. Lantern is unlit, faceplate alone gleams from exterior sunlight; maintain optical open space around it. Keep side-on platform edge horizontal and wall frontal. Only one reflector.
RIGHT TOP and RIGHT BOTTOM: Match each other and the tail in the reference. Each shows a SHORT EXPOSED TAPERING CURVED TAIL SECTION, thick base entering dark rubble on RIGHT, pointed end extending LEFT. It belongs to an enormous hidden animal. Grey-ivory, pale blue overlapping leaf-shaped scales flow in one direction. It lies horizontally and only curves gently; NOT an oval, round stone, egg, disconnected object, claw, face or snake animal. Two or three mossy stone blocks cover its base. In the TOP study, all tail scales are matte chalky grey and the tip rests heavily. In the BOTTOM study, ONE flush scale near the tapered tip softly glows pearl gold with tiny warm veins spreading through adjacent skin; the tip rises a barely visible amount to suggest its first breath, thick base stays buried. A single thin ray from off-frame left ends at this particular scale; do not illuminate every scale or make the tail a gold jewel. The overall silhouette remains the same in both.
Only these three studies, clean attractive production design board. No labels or written text, no arrows, no extra views, no large background scenery, no UI. Clearly drawn, easy to understand material construction, preserve reference art and species identity.
